items.q: Where is our Solar System located in the Milky Way?
items.correct: About two-thirds of the way out from the centre, in one of the spiral arms.
items.misconception: Right at the centre of the galaxy.
items.why: Students assume our Sun is central (Copernican habits die hard). We're in an unremarkable position about 26,000 light years from the centre, in the Orion Spur, a minor branch of the Milky Way.

items.q: What type of galaxy is the Milky Way?
items.why: Correct answer: Spiral. “Elliptical” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.
It's ~2.5 million light-years. “~100,000 light-years” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: Approximately how many light-years across is the Milky Way?
items.why: The real figure is 100000. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
